units.text: Under the Affordable Care Act (ACA), you don't have to pay a penalty for not having health insurance for 2019 or any year after that.

units.text: For 2018, if you were enrolled in VA health care, CHAMPVA, or certain other programs, you met the minimum essential coverage requirement and won't have to pay the fee.

units.text: The ACA doesn't change your VA health benefits or out-of-pocket costs.
supporting_chunk_ids: Affordable Care Act (ACA) And Your Coverage | Veterans Affairs#1_0::c0000

units.text: If you're not signed up for a VA or DoD health care program, you may be able to get coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace, Medicaid, or CHIP.
supporting_chunk_ids: Affordable Care Act (ACA) And Your Coverage | Veterans Affairs#1_0::c0000
units.reason: The context states 'You may be able to get coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace... or qualify for free or low-cost coverage through Medicaid or the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP).'
